result.summary: Applies two upstream backport patches to Cap'n Proto in depends to fix non-atomic reads in debug assertions. It replaces raw memory reads of mutex futex states and atomic reference counters with relaxed atomic loads.
result.problem: Unoptimized builds, including ThreadSanitizer (TSan) CI jobs, enable Cap'n Proto debug assertions that inspect mutex futex words and atomic reference counts non-atomically. When objects communicate across threads, TSan flags these debug reads as data races, failing CI runs.
evidence: PR description: 'The TSan job builds capnp without optimization, which automatically enables these assertions, and TSan reports these reads as data races the moment KJ objects start communicating across threads.'
Links to a concrete CI failure in bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#376 triggered by switching EventLoop::sync() to kj::Executor::executeSync().
Patches correspond directly to upstream Cap'n Proto backport commits b91a6ba7c7 and cc13c8c45f (capnproto/capnproto#2855).
result.scope_notes: Adds two patch files directly to depends/patches/capnp/ and updates depends/packages/capnp.mk to apply them during extraction.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided matches the previous description; no changes to the approach or commit contents.
result.card: Adds upstream Cap'n Proto patches to depends to fix non-atomic reads in mutex and reference count debug assertions. When capnp is compiled without optimization, such as in ThreadSanitizer CI runs, these non-atomic reads are reported as data races once objects communicate across threads. This fixes a TSan failure blocking bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#376.

risk.why: A flaw in the backported capnp patches could cause build failures or concurrency issues in experimental multiprocess builds.
